inputs.text: The turmoil involving the US, Israel and Iran is a reminder that ordinary Indian families bear the costs of an energy system built around imported crude and decisions they have no power to influence. Keeping petrol and diesel prices stable and cutting excise duties can protect households; blaming that support instead of confronting the dependence is a choice that shields the system, not the public. Energy security must mean a planned transition with workers and low-income families protected—not making them absorb the shocks and costs of reform.
